explanation: Heterochromatin is highly condensed and cannot be transcribed. In genetic female mammals (who inherit two X chromosomes), one of the two X chromosomes is permanently shut down in a process called X-inactivation, forming a highly condensed structure known as a Barr Body. This inactivation ensures dosage compensation, meaning that genetic males (who have only one X chromosome) and females produce equivalent amounts of gene products from X-linked genes. The choice of which X chromosome is inactivated (maternal or paternal) occurs randomly and independently in each embryonic cell. Consequently, if a female is heterozygous for a gene on the X chromosome, she will show a mosaic pattern of expression, where different cells express different alleles.

questions.q: Why is X-inactivation biologically important in mammals?
opts: It allows females to produce twice as many X-linked proteins as males.
It ensures that genetic males and females produce the same amount of gene products from X chromosome genes.
It prevents DNA replication errors during mitosis.
It triggers meiosis in female gametes.
